rows.title: Lamont to spare UConn, CSCU from required spending cuts
rows.standfirst: But to keep spending under CT’s constitutional cap, Lamont needs to find the $106M in savings required by the legislature somewhere else.

rows.title: Legislators mull how CT should react to One Big Beautiful Bill
rows.standfirst: To buffer the effects of the One Big Beautiful Bill, CT legislators are mulling adjustments to the spending cap and more.

rows.title: CT government’s struggles with overtime continue
rows.standfirst: Connecticut spent a record $316 million in overtime last fiscal year, but overall spending, adjusted for inflation, is down from 2011.

rows.title: Federal cutbacks could cost CT food stamp program $180M
rows.standfirst: The memorandum issued Friday did not project added costs tied to Medicaid that will pump nearly $7 billion in federal funds into CT this year.

rows.title: Sales tax holidays under fire as CT launches its promotion
rows.standfirst: CT’s sales tax holiday, from Sunday through Aug. 23, exempts clothing under $100 from the 6.35% sales tax. Some say it doesn’t do much good.

rows.title: Heating aid in CT expected to increase this winter
rows.standfirst: For the first time in four years, CT officials are anticipating an increase in energy assistance for low-income families this winter.

rows.title: CT’s coffers are swelling, but towns are feeling the pinch
rows.standfirst: Once inflation is taken into account, Connecticut municipalities are down almost $370 million, or 10%, in state funding since 2016.

rows.title: CT tax revenue surges — for 3rd time since state budget was set
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers, who watered down spending this spring thinking funds were unavailable, have learned CT has nearly $1.3B to spare.

rows.title: Report: CT has slashed deeply into hefty pension debt
rows.standfirst: In what was called ‘an astonishing turnaround,’ a Pew report found CT slashed its debt dramatically by pouring surplus dollars into pensions.
